patterns.name: Point cloud starter (boxPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Minimal POP chain — a single boxPOP generator wired into an outPOP terminator inside a baseCOMP wrapper. Useful as the first step when learning POPs, or as a sanity check that your bridge + create + connect tools work.
patterns.notes: boxPOP generates a 6-face box mesh as points + topology. outPOP marks the chain endpoint — required for the POP family to be cookable when wrapped in a COMP and used as a Geometry source.
pitfalls: To visualize, attach a popViewer (COMP) or wire into a Geometry COMP feeding a Render TOP — outPOP alone produces no rendered output.

patterns.name: Noise-displaced grid (gridPOP → noisePOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Generate a flat point grid, then modulate the P (position) attribute via noisePOP. Canonical recipe for procedural surface displacement and the foundation for most audio-reactive or time-driven POP looks.
patterns.notes: noisePOP reads the P attribute from upstream and additively perturbs it (default behavior). Tune amplitude/period via noisePOP's params. To drive the noise period from a CHOP, expose the param as Custom and bind to a CHOP via export — or use a choptoPOP upstream to feed values per-point.
pitfalls: noisePOP modifies P by default; if the upstream chain doesn't carry P (rare for generators, possible for filter-only chains), the noise output is undefined.
Animating period vs amplitude gives very different looks: animating period feels like 'morphing terrain', animating amplitude feels like 'breathing'.

patterns.name: CHOP → POP cross-family bridge (constantCHOP + choptoPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Convert a CHOP's channel values into POP points/attributes via choptoPOP. Foundation for audio-reactive POP work — replace constantCHOP with audiofilterCHOP / analyzeCHOP / fft outputs to drive POP attributes from sound.
patterns.notes: choptoPOP has ZERO wire inputs — the CHOP source is bound via the `chop` param as a relative or absolute op path. The `src` value here is a sibling-relative path that TD resolves against c2p's parent. This is the convention for ALL cross-family ingestion POPs (choptoPOP, toptoPOP, dattoPOP, soptoPOP).
pitfalls: Wiring a CHOP into choptoPOP via td_connect_ops will fail or silently no-op — choptoPOP has 0 inputConnectors. Use td_set_param chop=<path> instead.
Path is resolved against the choptoPOP's parent, not the project root. If you move the pattern into a different wrapper, the relative path stays valid; absolute paths don't.

patterns.name: TOP → POP cross-family bridge (noiseTOP + toptoPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Convert a TOP's pixels into POP points (one point per pixel or sampled subset). Foundation for depth-to-points work, video-reactive particles, and any workflow where the visual source lives in TOP space.
patterns.notes: toptoPOP follows the same param-not-wire convention as choptoPOP — the source TOP is bound via `input0top` (note the indexed naming, hinting at multi-TOP variants). Swap noiseTOP for a kinectTOP or realsenseTOP / nidepthTOP to get true depth-to-points; swap for a moviefileinTOP to get video-driven points.
pitfalls: toptoPOP has 0 inputConnectors. Use td_set_param input0top=<path>, NOT td_connect_ops.

Default sampling reads ALL pixels — at 1920×1080 that's 2M points, which can tank framerate. Downsample the source TOP (resolutionTOP) before feeding into toptoPOP for interactive work, or set toptoPOP's sampling/density params.
